nodes.description: The AP-4 adaptor complex associates with the trans-Golgi network and exports ATG9A from it; in AP-4-deficient cells that export fails, reducing ATG9A delivery to pre-autophagosomal structures and impairing autophagosome formation. All four AP-4 subunit genes are curated on this node because biallelic variants in any of them cause the same disease, AP-4-associated HSP, which this entry carries as a single subtype row. The node is kept separate from the endolysosomal membrane-traffic node because the characterised AP-4 defect is autophagosome biogenesis rather than endosomal transport.

nodes.description: A mechanism class shared by complex-HSP genes whose products act in endosomal sorting, endosome maturation and lysosomal transport. Spastizin (ZFYVE26) localizes partly to endoplasmic reticulum and endosomal compartments; spartin (SPART) resembles molecules of endosomal trafficking; VPS37A is a subunit of the ESCRT system that matures multivesicular bodies; and ATP13A2 is a lysosomal transport ATPase. The AP-4 adaptor complex is curated as its own node because its characterised defect is autophagosome formation rather than endosomal transport. Every gene bound here causes a complex HSP recorded on this entry, and the node's downstream edge records that failure feeding the pleiotropic SPG-protein dysfunction the entry models.

nodes.description: Calcium efflux from the endoplasmic reticulum into the cytoplasm is controlled by inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate binding to its receptor, and activated receptors are then degraded by the endoplasmic-reticulum-associated degradation pathway. Two complex-HSP genes on this entry act in that degradation step: ERLIN2, whose biallelic variants cause SPG18, and RNF170, the ubiquitin E3 ligase that targets the receptors and whose bi-allelic variants cause SPG85. The RNF170 report names inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate signalling as a candidate key pathway for the hereditary spastic paraplegias, which is the claim this node records.

nodes.description: Reduced head circumference. It recurs across unrelated complex forms on this entry rather than marking any one of them: the GPT2 Deficiency row records postnatal microcephaly in all affected individuals of the defining kindreds, the AR Complex HSP row names the AP-4-associated disorders as a childhood-onset complex form with severe developmental delay and microcephaly, and it was reported in both the NT5C2 family with a splice-donor variant and the kindred homozygous for the ARL6IP1 nonsense allele. nodes.description: A second recurrent mechanism class among complex-HSP genes, whose products are lipid-modifying enzymes. DDHD2 is an intracellular phospholipase A1 and its loss produces an abnormal cerebral lipid peak detectable by magnetic resonance spectroscopy; PNPLA6 encodes neuropathy target esterase, which maintains phospholipid homeostasis in the nervous system; ABHD16A is the main brain phosphatidylserine hydrolase; and B4GALNT1 loss abolishes synthesis of GM2 and the downstream complex gangliosides. Each of these genes causes a complex HSP recorded on this entry, and the DDHD2 report shows the lipid disturbance directly in patients by cerebral magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

nodes.description: In complex HSP the mutated SPG proteins have diverse housekeeping functions — axonal transport, endoplasmic reticulum tubular network morphogenesis, mitochondrial quality control, myelin formation, and endolysosomal/autophagic membrane trafficking. Loss of these functions injures neuronal and glial populations beyond the corticospinal tract (cortical neurons, cerebellar neurons, peripheral nerve, retina, and oligodendrocyte myelin), producing the additional "complicating" features (thin corpus callosum, cognitive decline, ataxia, neuropathy, retinopathy) that distinguish complex from pure HSP. This pleiotropy explains why complex forms cluster among loci with broad subcellular roles (e.g., SPG11/SPG15 endolysosomal-autophagy, SPG7 mitochondrial, SPG2/PLP1 myelin).

nodes.description: Three complex-HSP genes on this entry act in purine nucleotide metabolism rather than in membrane traffic, lipid metabolism, mitochondrial assembly or axonal transport: NT5C2, the cytosolic 5'-nucleotidase II that hydrolyses nucleoside monophosphates and whose biallelic variants cause SPG45; AMPD2, an AMP deaminase, mutated in SPG63; and ENTPD1, described by the same study as an extracellular enzyme that hydrolyses adenosine nucleotides in the synaptic cleft, mutated in SPG64. The exome study that identified all three placed them in one purine-metabolism module, which is why they are bound together here rather than on the pleiotropic node that holds the genes with diverse housekeeping roles. The node records the pathway the lesions fall in rather than a measured metabolite change; the sources cited here establish the genetic lesions and the enzymes' assigned pathway, and the modifier is therefore ABNORMAL rather than a direction.

nodes.description: ARL6IP1, the gene mutated in SPG61, is a tetraspan endoplasmic reticulum membrane protein whose reticulon-like short hairpin transmembrane domains shape high-curvature ER tubules; it binds atlastin, the GTPase that mediates formation of the tubular ER network and is itself mutated in SPG3A. The SPG61 allele cited at this node is a nonsense variant predicted to abolish the protein, so the lesion recorded here is loss of ER tubule shaping. It is kept separate from the IP3-receptor calcium-release node because ERLIN2 and RNF170 act on receptor degradation and ER calcium handling rather than on ER membrane geometry, and separate from the pleiotropic node because the mechanism here is a single named biophysical function rather than a diverse housekeeping role.
